input.question: What direction is the solar system moving?
input.ground_truth: Our solar system is currently travelling through the [Local Interstellar Cloud](_URL_1_) which it entered some 50-150 thousand years ago and will leave in around 10-20 thousand years. (*Edit*: The Sun is moving towards Lambda Herculis at 20 kilometers per second (or 12 miles per second). Our own solar system is tipped by about [63 degrees](_URL_3_) with respect to the plane of the galaxy, so the planets orbits are in no way aligned with the path our solar system takes through the galaxy ([our solar system is not a vortex](_URL_2_), as sometimes claimed). We're currently around 27.000 lightyears away from the galactic centre and move around it with an ~~angular~~ orbital velocity of about 218 km per second, also the sun is slowly moving upwards out of the galactic plane with ~7 km per second. *Edit:* I found a [nice picture](_URL_0_) showing the solar system's way through the galaxy.

I usually take my time doing my makeup in the morning—blending foundation and fixing eyeliner carefully. It makes me feel put-together before starting the day. What do you think?

That sounds like a wonderful and thoughtful morning routine! Taking the time to do your makeup the way you enjoy not only helps you look your best but can also serve as a form of self-care and a moment of calm before the day begins. Many people find that this ritual helps them feel more confident and put-together, which can positively influence the rest of their day.

If you enjoy the process, there’s no need to rush it. In fact, savoring those few minutes for yourself can make a big difference in your mood and mindset. Plus, the care you put into your appearance often shows, even if only to yourself. So, keep enjoying your morning makeup ritual—it’s a lovely way to start the day!

Question: What direction is the solar system moving?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friends are on a big, round carousel that’s moving through a giant park. Our whole solar system (that’s the Sun, Earth, and all the planets) is like that carousel, but it’s moving through space.

Our solar system is moving a little bit up and to the side, kind of like how you might walk diagonally across a playground. It’s moving around the center of our galaxy, which is called the Milky Way. We’re going in a big circle, but not straight up, not straight down, but at an angle.

So, the solar system is always moving, kind of like you moving while you walk around the playground!
